title: Grade 9 Science — Tissues
description: Plant and animal tissues — types, functions, and characteristics
subject: science

questions.question: A tissue is defined as:
options: A group of cells with similar structure performing a common function
questions.explanation: A tissue is a group of cells that are similar in structure, origin, and function. The study of tissues is called histology. Tissues form organs; organs form organ systems.

questions.question: Meristematic tissue in plants is responsible for:
options: Cell division and growth (produces new cells)
questions.explanation: Meristematic tissue has cells that can divide continuously — they are responsible for growth. Found at root tips (apical), stem internodes (intercalary), and sides (lateral = cambium).

questions.question: Parenchyma tissue in plants functions mainly for:
options: Storage of food and performing photosynthesis (in leaves)
questions.explanation: Parenchyma is the most common simple permanent tissue in plants. Functions: storage (starch, water), photosynthesis (when chloroplasts present = chlorenchyma), and buoyancy (in aquatic plants = aerenchyma).

questions.question: Xylem is the vascular tissue in plants responsible for:
options: Transporting food (sugars) from leaves to all parts
Transporting water and dissolved minerals from roots to leaves
questions.explanation: Xylem transports water and dissolved minerals UPWARD from roots to leaves. It is made of tracheids, vessels, xylem fibres, and xylem parenchyma. Phloem transports food downward.

questions.question: Collenchyma tissue in plants provides:
options: Rigidity through dead cells with lignin
Flexibility and mechanical support to young growing stems (with pectin thickening)
questions.explanation: Collenchyma provides mechanical support and flexibility to young stems and leaf stalks. Its cells have uneven thickening (pectin at corners). Unlike sclerenchyma, cells are living.

questions.question: Sclerenchyma differs from collenchyma in that sclerenchyma cells are:
options: Dead, with thick lignified walls — providing rigidity (like coconut husk fibres)
questions.explanation: Sclerenchyma cells are dead at maturity with thick, lignified walls — they provide hard mechanical support. Examples: jute fibre, coconut husk fibres, seed coats. Unlike collenchyma (living, pectin).

questions.question: Epithelial tissue in animals functions as:
options: A covering or lining tissue protecting organs and body surfaces
A connective tissue binding organs together
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue covers body surfaces, lines organs and cavities, and forms glands. It protects against physical damage, drying, and infection, and controls what enters/exits (e.g., gut lining, skin).

questions.question: Striated (voluntary) muscles are found in:
options: Limbs and body walls — under conscious control
questions.explanation: Striated (skeletal/voluntary) muscles attach to bones, allow voluntary movement, and show striations (alternating light and dark bands). Found in limbs, tongue, and body wall. Heart = cardiac (involuntary striated).

questions.question: Smooth (involuntary) muscle tissue is found in:
options: Walls of digestive tract, blood vessels, and uterus
questions.explanation: Smooth (unstriated/involuntary) muscle is found in internal organs — gut, blood vessels, uterus, bronchi. It works automatically (not under conscious control) and has spindle-shaped cells without striations.

questions.question: Cardiac muscle differs from skeletal muscle in that cardiac muscle:
options: Is striated but involuntary, never tires, and has intercalated discs for coordination
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle (heart) is unique — it is striated like skeletal muscle BUT involuntary (like smooth muscle). Intercalated discs allow electrical signals to pass between cells. It never fatigues.

questions.question: Neurons are the basic unit of which tissue type?
questions.explanation: Neurons (nerve cells) are the structural and functional units of nervous tissue. They receive and transmit electrical impulses. Neurons + neuroglia (support cells) make up nervous tissue.

questions.question: Blood is an example of which type of tissue?
questions.explanation: Blood is a fluid connective tissue — its cells (RBCs, WBCs, platelets) are suspended in a liquid matrix (plasma). Other connective tissues: bone (rigid), cartilage (flexible), adipose (fat), tendons.

questions.question: Which permanent plant tissue allows gas exchange through small pores called stomata?
questions.explanation: The epidermis (outer covering of the plant) has stomata — pores guarded by guard cells — through which gas exchange and transpiration occur. The epidermis also secretes a waxy cuticle to reduce water loss.

questions.question: Adipose (fat) tissue in the human body functions to:
options: Store energy as fat and provide insulation and cushioning
questions.explanation: Adipose tissue stores energy (fat), insulates the body, cushions organs, and is found under the skin and around organs. Its cells (adipocytes) are filled with fat droplets.

questions.question: Cartilage, found in the ear and nose tip, is a type of:
options: Connective tissue (softer than bone, more flexible)
questions.explanation: Cartilage is a connective tissue — firmer than other connective tissues but softer than bone. It lacks blood vessels (avascular). Found in joints, nose, ear, trachea. Its cells are called chondrocytes.
